inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are RMB, so WACC is built in RMB: China 10y CGB ~1.8% + beta ~1.2 x China ERP ~6.8% = ~10.0% cost of equity. Company is net cash with only USD197m-equivalent short-term bank debt at 2.11%, so WACC = cost of equity = 10.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and the box-office slump are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease payments (~0.7% of revenue, sized to the new office lease that took lease liabilities from RMB10.3m to RMB137.4m at 2026-06-30) are deducted via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI is RMB7.7m (2026-06-30) and deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: online movie/performance ticketing, film promotion/distribution and content investment, advertising -- routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with owner-fcf-adaptations). First valuation of this ticker; no prior model to match. Base revenue is FY2025 (RMB4,631.5m, a Ne Zha 2 boosted box-office year). FY2026 year-one is anchored to H1 FY2026 actuals (revenue RMB1,789.8m, -27.6% YoY; EBITDA RMB24.9m; national box office -40.6%) and an H2 roughly flat on H2 FY2025 (~RMB2.0bn). No formal guidance is given; the interim outlook only cites 2026 cumulative box office of RMB26.4bn at report date. D&A (0.35% of revenue) is economic D&A only -- PPE depreciation plus non-acquired intangible amortisation; the ~RMB89m/yr amortisation of business-combination intangibles is excluded so no finite tax shelter is perpetuated, and cash tax is effectively charged on owner EBITDA. Capex is tiny (RMB5.7m FY2025); the real reinvestment is film prepayments/rights, which run through EBITDA via impairments and through working capital. wc_capture is set to 0: history shows film prepayments are a cash use in both up and down years (FY2024 revenue -14% with FCF -RMB861m), so a growth-linked capture would wrongly release cash in the FY2026 decline. Interest income (RMB62.1m FY2025) is stripped from owner FCF because net cash plus treasury bonds and wealth-management products sit in the bridge. Buybacks: only FY2024 (RMB45.6m); the flat share count is a modelling convention, not something the company funds annually -- it paid its first dividend (RMB263m) in FY2025. SBC is small but non-zero (0.5% of revenue), so the house/street band is narrow but not collapsed.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.0-4.3%) diverges massively from revenue (26-28%) and EPS CAGRs. Revenue/EPS/FCF CAGRs start from COVID-depressed FY2020 and the weak FY2022 base and end in the Ne Zha 2 boosted FY2025; they are base-period artefacts of a hit-driven, box-office-cyclical business, not trend growth. Revenue has oscillated RMB3.3-4.8bn since FY2019 with no trend.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY2020 193.1, FY2021 497.9, FY2022 14.8, FY2023 1,359.8, FY2024 -1,020.6, FY2025 1,104.3 (RMB m). FCF CAGRs are meaningless given sign changes and working-capital swings from film prepayments; five-year cumulative owner FCF FY2021-25 is ~RMB1.96bn (~RMB390m/yr). SBC has fallen from RMB184m (FY2017) to RMB25m, so the SBC adjustment shrinks over time rather than growing.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue ~RMB3.8bn (-18%) on the 40% box-office slump with EBITDA ~8% after H1's near-zero; FY2027 recovers to ~RMB4.25bn, below the FY2023/FY2025 peaks, and grows low-single-digit thereafter. EBITDA margin returns to 17%, just under the FY2019/FY2021-25 average of ~17.7% that includes FY2024's 7.9% trough. PRC cash tax 26% (statutory 25% with non-deductibles; GAAP ETR 27% FY2025).

bull.narrative: Box office normalises back to the RMB50bn+ range from FY2027 and live-performance ticketing (national performance box office +9.4% in H1 2026) keeps compounding; Maoyan's lead-distribution record (top-two Spring Festival film six years running) converts into higher-margin content wins. Margin settles at 20%, between FY2019/FY2025 and the FY2023 peak of 25.6%.

bear.narrative: The 2026 attendance collapse (moviegoers -34%) proves structural: short-video and micro-drama substitution keep cinema attendance in decline, Douyin and Alibaba's Taopiaopiao squeeze ticketing commissions, and content investments keep throwing off impairments (RMB81.9m net impairment on financial assets in H1 2026 alone). Revenue stalls near RMB3.6-4.0bn and margin caps at 12%, closer to the FY2022/FY2024 troughs than the peaks.

scenario_narratives.base: Cyclical trough, not structural break: FY2026 is a box-office down-year after the Ne Zha 2 peak (H1 national box office -40.6%, Maoyan revenue -27.6%, near-breakeven EBITDA), FY2027 recovers partially and the business returns to its long-run ~17% EBITDA margin on ~RMB4.3-4.9bn revenue. Ticketing remains anchored by the WeChat/QQ traffic relationship with Tencent; live-performance ticketing grows ahead of film; content wins and losses roughly average out as they have over FY2019-25.
scenario_narratives.bull: China box office rebounds to RMB50bn+ and offline performance keeps growing high-single-digit; Maoyan's distribution franchise (Pegasus, six straight years with a top-two Spring Festival film) and IP/derivative operations lift margin to ~20%. The large net-cash and investment balance (~RMB3.1bn against a ~RMB3.6bn market cap) supports dividends and buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bear: Cinema attendance is in structural decline as short video and micro-dramas take leisure time; ticketing commissions erode under Douyin/Taopiaopiao competition and dependence on Tencent's traffic terms; content investment keeps producing impairments. Revenue stalls and margin caps at 12%. Even here the business stays cash-generative and the balance sheet is not at risk.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the 2026 attendance drop (-34%) may be structural rather than cyclical and Maoyan's ticketing depends on a single traffic partner (Tencent). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs both a box-office rebound and sustained content hits. Base 50%: the FY2019-25 record shows the business mean-reverts to mid-to-high-teens margins after troughs.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Maoyan is a hit-driven, box-office-cyclical ticketing and film-distribution platform priced near its net cash and investments. The valuation charges the FY2026 trough explicitly in year one, normalises to the historical average margin, deducts the seasonal box-office float and the declared dividend from June cash, and adds treasury bonds, wealth-management products and strategic stakes at carrying value. The weighted value says the market is pricing a near-permanent bear case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Structural decline in China cinema attendance (2026 moviegoers -34% YoY) rather than a cyclical trough
Dependence on Tencent (WeChat/QQ) traffic for ticketing; renegotiated terms would compress margin
Content and co-investment impairments; RMB4.66bn intangibles (largely goodwill) at risk of write-down
Ticketing competition from Douyin and Alibaba Pictures/Taopiaopiao
Cayman/VIE structure and PRC regulatory risk on entertainment content
Bridge relies on the June 2026 balance sheet adjusted for seasonal float; the true year-end float and scrip take-up may differ
CNY/HKD rate is not refreshed by refresh_price.py
